topics.title: Environmental Performance Index
bullets: India has been ranked 176th out of 177 countries in the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2026, with a score of 22.46 out of 100 .
The country is second lowest globally, ahead of only Laos (177th), and last among 8 South Asian nations .
Estonia topped the index with a score of 74.79, followed by Luxembourg, the United Kingdom, Finland, and the Netherlands . Background –
The EPI is a biennial global index ranking countries on environmental performance, serving as a sustainability "scorecard".
It was initiated in 2000 under the initial name Environmental Sustainability Index (ESI).
It evaluates countries using 47 indicators across 12 categories under three objectives: Environmental Health, Ecosystem Vitality, and Climate Change.
Environmental Health (25% weight) : Measures air quality, water quality, and sanitation, including indicators like ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) levels .

Ecosystem Vitality (45% weight) : Assesses how well countries manage their natural resources, including tree cover loss, pesticide pollution risks, marine habitat protection, and grassland conversion (a new indicator for 2026) .
Climate Change Mitigation (30% weight) : Tracks progress on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, including CO2 and methane emission trends .
The EPI is published by the Yale Center for Environmental Law & Policy (YCELP) at Yale University and the Center for International Earth Science Information Network (CIESIN) at Columbia University .
The research team is led by Daniel C. Esty, Director of YCELP, along with Z. A. Wendling, J. W. Emerson, A. de Sherbinin, and others .
The EPI is funded by the McCall MacBain Foundation, which supports the work at both Yale and Columbia . India’s Ranking –
India has remained among the five worst-performing countries since 2022, with its rank improving slightly from the absolute bottom in 2022 to second-last .
The 2026 ranking shows a slight improvement of +7.47 over the last decade, but progress has been slow .
Environmental Health: Ranked 174th – reflecting severe air quality and pollution challenges .
Ecosystem Vitality: Ranked 171st – indicating weak natural resource management and biodiversity protection .
Climate Change Mitigation: Ranked 130th – a relatively better performance, but still far from global leaders .
India ranked 175th globally in air quality, reflecting the burden of death and disease from PM2.5 exposure .
Carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide exposures over the past decade have shown negative values, indicating deteriorating conditions .

The report noted that India faces an "acute development-versus- pollution tension" as hundreds of millions gain access to modern energy services but at the cost of serious urban air pollution and spiking GHG emissions .
India's Marine Protected Area (MPA) effectiveness was recorded at a negative -51.77, reflecting a collapse in marine conservation effectiveness .
India has also been marked down for tree cover loss, pesticide pollution risks, and inadequate biodiversity protections .
The EPI noted that India's weak performance reflects continued reliance on coal-fired power and lack of biodiversity protections .
India's per-capita emissions remain relatively low by global standards, but they are growing rapidly .
Hundreds of millions of citizens are only now gaining reliable access to electricity, which is still substantially dependent on coal- fired electricity.
This creates a fundamental tension between development and environmental protection, a dilemma the EPI report itself acknowledges . Other Ranks –
Estonia topped the index with a score of 74.79, followed by Luxembourg (2nd) , United Kingdom (3rd) , Finland (4th) , and Netherlands (5th) .
European countries hold all but one of the top 20 positions, reflecting strong performance on environmental health and climate change mitigation .
The UK moved up from 5th in 2024 to 3rd in 2026, while Japan (16th) was the only non-European country in the top 20 .
Laos ranked 177th (last) with a score of 21.78 .
India ranked 176th with a score of 22.46 .
Bangladesh ranked 175th, completing the bottom three in South Asia .
Pakistan ranked 133rd with a score of 45.1, the highest in South Asia.
Sri Lanka ranked 139th, Nepal ranked 151st, Afghanistan ranked 154th.
India is 7th among 8 South Asian countries, ahead of only Laos globally, and has been among the five worst-performing countries since 2022 .
China climbed to 129th position, up from near the bottom in previous years, after removing many coal-fired power plants near major cities .
China's improvement reflects significant environmental actions in the last few years .
The United States was ranked 27th, slipping from previous positions .
The MoEFCC has questioned EPI methodology, arguing it ignores India's development stage, population size, and historical emissions.
India earlier dismissed the 2022 ranking (last place) as based on "surmises and unscientific methods" .

The government argues the EPI fails to account for Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) , recognizing developed countries' greater historical responsibility for environmental degradation.
EPI researchers state that the index measures the current state of environmental conditions rather than future policy promises .
The EPI aims to inform real-time policy choices rather than assigning historical blame .
Yale researchers welcomed collaboration with India to improve the index, emphasizing that the EPI is a "scorecard" that highlights leaders and laggards .
Experts recommend India build credible environmental data infrastructure to hold itself accountable and contest rankings with evidence, not denial.
A more useful approach is engaging with EPI authors while strengthening domestic metrics, rather than outright rejection.
This would help track progress in air quality, marine governance, grassland protection, and renewable energy transition.

topics.title: Ceuta Migrant Crisis
bullets: Between 30 and 31 July 2026, an estimated 60,000 to 80,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, marking the largest surge of irregular arrivals on EU territory in such a short span .
At least 72 migrants died on the Spanish side of the border, with 11 deaths reported in Morocco .
Spain deployed army units to support border security, and over 70,000 migrants were returned to Morocco within days, but 862 unaccompanied minors remain stranded in Ceuta . Background –
Ceuta is a small Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa, separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar .
It shares an 8-kilometre land border with Morocco, making it one of only two land borders between the EU and Africa .
With a population of approximately 84,000, Ceuta has been under Spanish rule for over 500 years .
Ceuta was conquered by Portugal in 1415 and came under Spanish rule in 1580 when the Portuguese and Spanish crowns were united .
After Portugal regained independence in 1640, Ceuta chose to remain loyal to Spain, a decision formalised in the Treaty of Lisbon in 1668 .
Morocco has never accepted Spain's sovereignty over Ceuta, claiming the territory since its independence from France in 1956, but the citizens of Ceuta overwhelmingly wish to remain Spanish .
Spain controls two enclaves on the North African coast: Ceuta and Melilla, along with several rocky islands known as the Plazas de Soberanía .
Melilla was conquered by Spain in 1497, predating Ceuta's incorporation into Spain .
In 1975, Morocco organised the "Green March" – a mass civilian march of 350,000 volunteers into the Spanish Sahara to force Spain to hand over the territory, which it did that same year.
Morocco argues that Ceuta and Melilla are integral parts of Moroccan territory because they lie on the African continent .
Spain, however, maintains that Ceuta has belonged to Spain long before the creation of the modern Moroccan state .
Spain argues that its sovereignty rests on centuries of continuous administration, whereas Morocco disputes Spanish sovereignty and continues to claim Ceuta and Melilla.
Ceuta has experienced multiple mass migration events over the years, with the 2026 surge being the largest .
In May 2021, between 8,000 and 10,000 migrants entered Ceuta over two days, widely interpreted as Morocco loosening border controls to pressure Spain .
In June 2022, an attempt by about 2,000 migrants to scale the Melilla border fence left at least 23 people dead .
Spain has constructed a sophisticated border system along the 8 km frontier, consisting of double six-metre-high fences, surveillance cameras, motion sensors, and floodlights .
The fences were initially built in the early 1990s and reinforced in 1995 and 2005, with significant EU financial contributions .
The border has become a symbol of "Fortress Europe" and the EU's efforts to manage migration . Recent News –
In April 2026, Spain's regularisation scheme for undocumented migrants attracted 1.2 million applications, which some EU states called a "pull factor".
On 29 June 2026, Spain's Supreme Court restricted the use of immediate returns in certain categories of maritime interception, strengthening procedural safeguards.
PM Sánchez said trafficking networks twisted the ruling into a rumour that Spain's doors were now open.
Between 30 and 31 July 2026, an estimated 60,000 to 80,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta, amounting to nearly 70% of the city's population .
Most of those entering Ceuta were young men, but there were also women, children, and even babies in the crowds .
At least 7,000 minors were among those who crossed illegally in the initial surge .
At least 72 migrants died on the Spanish side of the border, with 11 deaths reported in Morocco .
Many drowned near the breakwater, while others were crushed in the crowd at the border fence .
A 17-year-old girl from Tangier told AP that she saw Spanish police pulling the body of her eight-year-old brother from the sea when she made it to shore .
Spain deployed army units to support the Guardia Civil at the border, and by Friday evening, most of those who had crossed had been sent back to Morocco .
Over 70,000 people voluntarily returned to Morocco after finding no food or shelter .
Spain's Interior Minister said he was working "firmly" with Morocco to avoid further "violations" of Spain's borders .
Over 862 unaccompanied minors remain stranded in Ceuta, creating an overcrowding rate of nearly 3,000% over the "standard capacity" of 29 .
The Spanish government has allocated 25 million euros to assist minors in Ceuta . Legal Framework –
Under Article 35 of Spain's 2000 foreigners' law, unaccompanied minors must be granted protection and receive "immediate attention" from Spanish child protection services .
The Spanish government has stated that the rights of all migrants, especially minors, are being respected during the crisis .
A Spanish National Court judge has ordered an investigation into whether the mass entry was an "action orchestrated" by criminal organisations .
The Schengen Area is a system of open borders spanning 29 European countries that have abolished controls at their common borders .
Ceuta is not part of the Schengen Area, meaning travellers between Ceuta and mainland Spain undergo separate border checks .
Italy's suspension of Schengen with Spain is a rare use of the provision allowing member states to reintroduce border controls in exceptional circumstances . EU –
The EU was born out of a post-WWII vision to secure lasting peace in Europe, ending centuries of bloody conflict between nations like France and Germany .

The first concrete step was the creation of the European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) in 1951, which pooled the coal and steel resources of six countries to prevent any one from making weapons of war .
The Treaties of Rome (1957) expanded this cooperation, establishing the European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom) .
1973 – The first enlargement saw Denmark, Ireland, and the UK join the Communities .
1985-1995 – The Schengen Agreement abolished internal borders , and the Maastricht Treaty (1992) formally created the European Union (EU) .
2002 – Euro notes and coins were introduced, replacing national currencies in the euro area .
European Parliament – represents EU citizens, is directly elected, and shares legislative power with the Council .
European Commission – is the EU's main executive body, proposing new laws and ensuring member countries apply them correctly .
European Council – consists of the heads of state or government of EU countries and defines the EU's general political direction and priorities .
The Schengen Area is the world's largest free travel area, guaranteeing free movement to over 450 million citizens .
It currently comprises 29 countries, including 25 EU member states and 4 non-EU countries like Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein .
In 2025, Bulgaria and Romania became fully part of the Schengen area, removing checks at internal land borders .
The EU's migration and asylum system was recently overhauled by the Pact on Migration and Asylum, which entered into application on 12 June 2026 .
A new five-year strategy was adopted in January 2026, focusing on preventing illegal migration, protecting those fleeing war, and attracting talent to the EU .

The strategy includes the use of digitalisation and AI to improve the speed and quality of asylum and migration management . Passage: A major Spain–Morocco crisis unfolded around Ceuta in late July 2026 after tens of thousands of migrants attempted to enter the Spanish-administered North African territory by land and sea. Many reportedly acted on false social-media claims that reaching Ceuta would guarantee asylum or access to a Spanish regularisation programme. The sudden movement overwhelmed border infrastructure and produced a serious humanitarian emergency, with numerous deaths and hundreds of unaccompanied minors left stranded. Spanish authorities alleged that inadequate Moroccan border enforcement had enabled the mass crossing, while some officials suspected that migration pressure was being used for geopolitical leverage. Morocco’s precise role remained disputed, but the episode revived longstanding tensions over Ceuta’s status and Spain’s relations with Rabat. Spain installed a floating maritime barrier and reinforced security around the enclave as European Union governments debated a coordinated response. Source: The Indian Express
